title: Google Empowers Gemini to Control Your Mac: New AI Feature Unveiled on TechCrunch
body:
Google unveiled a major upgrade to its Gemini AI platform on Thursday, extending the service’s capabilities beyond conversational assistance to direct interaction with macOS. The new Gemini desktop app can now navigate native Mac applications, organize files, complete forms and execute multi‑step workflows on a user’s behalf, effectively turning the AI into a hands‑free productivity partner for Mac users.

The feature, dubbed “Gemini Agent,” leverages Google’s recent advances in large‑language models and multimodal reasoning to interpret natural‑language commands and translate them into concrete actions within the operating system. Users can, for example, ask Gemini to “file all receipts from the past month into a folder labeled ‘Expenses 2024’” or “populate this spreadsheet with the sales figures from the last quarter,” and the AI will locate the relevant documents, open the appropriate apps, and perform the required edits. The system also supports more complex sequences, such as “draft an email to the marketing team, attach the latest campaign brief, and schedule it for send at 9 a.m. tomorrow,” demonstrating a blend of content generation and UI automation.

Google positions this development as a response to growing competition in the AI‑assistant market, where Apple’s Siri, Microsoft’s Copilot, and various third‑party bots have begun to offer deeper integration with desktop environments. By allowing Gemini to act directly within macOS, Google aims to differentiate its offering through a combination of sophisticated language understanding and tight coupling with Google’s own cloud services. The company notes that the agent runs locally on the Mac, with only the inference engine communicating with Google’s servers, a design intended to address privacy concerns while still delivering up‑to‑date model improvements.

Industry analysts see the move as both an opportunity and a risk. On the positive side, automating repetitive tasks could free up significant amounts of time for professionals who juggle spreadsheets, emails and document management daily. Early testers reported noticeable gains in efficiency, especially when handling bulk operations that would otherwise require manual sorting and copy‑pasting. However, critics warn that granting an AI the ability to control a user’s computer raises security and accountability questions. Google has emphasized that Gemini Agent requires explicit user permission for each action, and that a transparent activity log will be available to review what the AI has done. Nonetheless, the potential for misuse—whether through malicious prompts or inadvertent errors—remains a concern that regulators and enterprises will likely scrutinize.

The rollout will begin with a beta program for select Mac users, with a wider public release slated for early 2027. Google plans to expand the agent’s reach to other operating systems, including Windows and Linux, later in the year, and to integrate deeper with Google Workspace tools such as Docs, Sheets and Drive. The company also hinted at future enhancements that could allow Gemini to interact with third‑party applications via APIs, opening the door to a broader ecosystem of AI‑driven automation.

If the Gemini Agent lives up to its promise, it could redefine how professionals approach everyday computing tasks, shifting the paradigm from manual input to conversational command. As AI continues to blur the line between software and assistant, the success of Google’s initiative will hinge on striking a balance between convenience, security and user trust. The coming months will reveal whether Gemini can become a reliable co‑pilot for Mac users or if the challenges of autonomous desktop operation prove too steep to overcome.
